fn.en: Tell a short story about something that happened to you, and react to someone else’s.

items.q: Last Saturday I ___ to a friend’s dinner. (go)
On the bus I ___ my old teacher. (see)
I ___ a present for her on the way. (buy)
We ___ at a small Italian place. (eat)
I ___ home at eleven. (leave)
I ___ it was a great evening. (think)

sub.en: Look at the pairs. Do irregular verbs take -ed in the past?

items.q: I ___ to the cinema yesterday.
items.why: Irregular verbs never take -ed. You learn each pair: go → went.

items.q: She ___ a taxi in the end.
We ___ a great time.
He ___ me the whole story.
They ___ us a present.
I ___ my keys under the sofa.

items.from: I go to the cinema every Friday.
items.a: I went to the cinema last Friday

items.from: She buys a coffee on the way to work.

items.a: We had dinner at eight last night

items.a: I met my friends two days ago

After that it started to rain
In the end I walked home

acts.title: Three days that went wrong
text: Aliya: Last Saturday I had my class dinner. First I couldn’t find my shoes, so I wore my old ones. Then the bus was late — I waited half an hour and it never came. After that it started to rain, so I called a taxi. In the end I walked home. I was so wet!

Timur: I got up at six for a job interview. I took the wrong bus and arrived an hour late. The manager said nothing, but I knew it was finished. In the end they gave me the job. I still don’t know why.

Dana: We went to the airport at four in the morning. My husband left the passports at home. He drove back, but the traffic was terrible. We missed the plane and bought new tickets. It was an expensive day.

items.s: Aliya found her shoes in the end.
Timur arrived late for the interview.
Dana and her husband caught their plane.

acts.title: Three days that went wrong
text: Aliya: … I waited half an hour and it never came. In the end I walked home. I was so wet!
Timur: … The manager said nothing, but I knew it was finished.
Dana: … We missed the plane and bought new tickets. It was an expensive day.

items.q: Aliya used this word after “in the” to mean “at last”.
Timur used the past of “know”.
Dana used the past of “buy”.
Dana used the past of “miss”. It ends in -ed.
Aliya used the past of “wait”. It ends in -ed.

tts: Responding to good news: That’s brilliant! That’s great! That’s amazing!
Responding to bad news: That’s terrible! That’s awful! What a nightmare! Oh no! Poor you!
Responding to interesting news: Really? That’s interesting!

“I waited an hour and the bus never came.”
“I met my old teacher on the bus.”

You want to start your story about last Saturday.

In the end I couldn’t find my shoes.

You finish your story: you walked all the way home.
o: In the end I walked home.
Then in the end after that I walked home.

write.q: Write your own “the day it all went wrong” story: 6 sentences. Use first, then, after that and in the end, and at least four irregular past verbs.
write.model: Last Monday I had an important meeting. First I got up late, because my phone was off. Then I took the wrong bus and I didn’t know where I was. After that it started to rain and I left my umbrella at home. I came to the office an hour late. In the end my manager said nothing — the meeting was on Tuesday.

speak.q: Tell your story out loud with first, then, after that, in the end. Then react to this: “I waited two hours at the airport and the flight was cancelled.”
speak.model: Last Monday I got up late. Then I took the wrong bus… In the end I came an hour late. — Oh no! What a nightmare. Poor you!
